changelog.change: Turned the time-trial Mode on in ui.enabledModes.
changelog.why: Row 23 - the Time Trial ships, so the last coming-soon tile on the Home becomes a button and every Mode this game promised is now playable. timeTrial.durationSec is untouched at the 120 it was minted with in Row 7 and gets its first reader here: two minutes is long enough that the ring of six Games deals more than one kind of board inside a run, so the sprint is a test of breadth rather than of one mechanic, and short enough that a player who has three minutes can finish one and still see their record move. It is a knob rather than a constant because it is the length of a contest, and a best run is recorded against the length it was set at - so shortening or lengthening the sprint starts a new record rather than invalidating the old one. Nothing else in this file moves: the Mode deals from the Row 22 pools, so it reads daily.games and infinite.defaultDifficulty exactly as the Infinite stream does, and adds no roster of its own.

changelog.change: Turned the infinite Mode on in ui.enabledModes.
changelog.why: Row 22 - the Infinite Mode ships, so its Home card stops being a coming-soon tile and becomes a button. Nothing else in this file moves, and that is the point of the shape it already had: infinite.lruWindow and infinite.defaultDifficulty were minted with the core knobs in Row 7 and get their first reader here, unchanged. The window is 200 picks and it is honest at that size because of what the pool is - the Mode rotates the six Games in daily.games and each of them holds 100 boards per band, so a stream filtered to one difficulty still draws from 565 distinct boards, nearly three times the window. defaultDifficulty is medium because a stream a player did not choose a setting for should open where the Daily's middle slot does. The Games the pool is baked for are daily.games itself rather than a second roster: it is already the answer to which Games are live, and a separate list would let a Game be dealt by one Mode and not the other for no reason a player could see, or let the stream ask for a pool nobody baked.

changelog.change: Turned the journey Mode on in ui.enabledModes and added ui.defaultJourney naming the path it opens.
changelog.why: Row 17 - the Journey Mode ships, so the Home card stops being a coming-soon tile and becomes a button. defaultJourney is a knob rather than a constant in the Mode for the reason every asset path in this repo is one: a Journey is content, more than one can ship at once, and which path a player lands on is a curation decision that must not need a code change. It is required rather than optional-with-a-default because a default would put the name of one particular content file inside the schema, which is exactly the hardcoding the field exists to remove. Nothing about the Daily moves: the two Modes share the Games and the runtime and share no state at all, and a Journey draws from each Game's ordinary wordlist against a ledger of its own, so turning this on cannot change a single baked day.

changelog.change: Added word-ladder to daily.games, keeping the ring alphabetical; daily.themedGames is unchanged.
changelog.why: Row 16 - the sixth Game reaches players. The ring stays in alphabetical order because that is what the workload measurement still prefers: counted as answers per board, alphabetical gives days of 7, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 10, a spread of three, and no permutation of the six beats it - the same criterion, and the same arithmetic, that chose the order when the ring replaced daily.mix. The themed ring is deliberately NOT widened, and that is a measurement rather than a symmetry: themed-nature holds 429 rows, and a ladder needs an add-one-ezhuthu chain THROUGH the set it is drawn from, so the question is not whether the theme has enough words but whether its words sit one letter apart. They do not. Over all 429 rows the theme's graph has 5 edges in total, 5 rows can climb a single rung, and ZERO can climb the three the easiest band asks for - so registering this Game against the theme would have made every themed day unbuildable rather than making it a ladder. That failure is silent by design: theme_can_fill answers no and the date falls back to the ordinary ring, so the cost would have been the loss of themed days, not a crash. hints.perGame gains no entry either: this Game bakes no rungs, its help is a play-time reveal priced in the rung it hands over, and a missing entry already reads as an allowance of zero.

changelog.change: Replaced daily.mix with daily.games and daily.themedGames.
changelog.why: Rows 18 to 21 shipped four more Games and every one of them stayed dark, because a mix of {anagram: 3} is the only shape a fixed per-Game count can take on a three-item day: five Games do not fit in three slots, so a mix that names them all is impossible and a mix that names three leaves two unreachable forever. games is a RING instead, and a day takes the playlist-length window that starts at its own date - so every Game comes round within one turn of the ring, consecutive days share only the Game the window carries over, and no day ever holds the same Game twice. Its ORDER decides which Games co-occur rather than which comes first (that is dailyRank, in the generator registry), and this order was chosen by measuring what a day asks of a player: counted as answers per board it gives days of 7, 7, 8, 8 and 11 answers, against 3 to 11 for the ramp order, so no day is a slog and none is over in a minute. themedGames is a SECOND ring, and the reason it exists is the whole reason daily.mix was never widened before: a themed day needs every Game in it to register the same theme AND to be able to build a puzzle from that theme's few hundred rows, so widening one ring to five would have turned every themed day off in silence. Measured against themed-nature's 429 rows, the anagram and the missing-letters board each fill it honestly for 62 consecutive themed days - more than a year at one a week - while the wordle runs dry after 37 (its easy bucket holds two words), the search board repeats an already-served word on the third themed day, and the crossword cannot build a single board from the set. So the themed ring holds the two that can, and it is allowed to be shorter than the playlist and deal one of them twice: an ordinary day's claim is variety of Games, a themed day's claim is that its words belong together, and padding a theme with an off-theme word to reach three Games would break the only claim that matters.

Row 19 - the wordle ladder is two rungs rather than three, and this allowance is the ceiling on how many a day may bake. The missing rung is firstEzhuthu, refused for the opposite reason to the missing-letters board's: there the answer's other ezhuthu are already printed, here the player can buy the same fact by spending a guess - and one guess answers five other positions at the same time, so the rung is strictly worse than the move it competes with. daily.mix is again deliberately NOT changed, on Row 18's terms: widening it without a matching themed set silently turns every themed day off.

Row 18 - this allowance caps how many rungs a day may bake for a Game, and the missing-letters ladder is two rungs rather than three. It is not a smaller budget for the same ladder: the first-ezhuthu rung cannot exist on a board that has already printed every ezhuthu it is not hiding, because the rung would either charge for a fact on the screen or be the answer. daily.mix is deliberately NOT changed in the same edit - see the PR - so nothing about today's Daily moves.

Row 14 of the lexicon pipeline - the anagram ladder is now three rungs (category, first ezhuthu, meaning) and this allowance is what caps how many a day may bake. Left at 2 the dearest rung, the one that says what the word means, would never reach a puzzle. It is a ceiling rather than a promise: a rung a word cannot honestly answer is skipped, so most days still bake two.

changelog.change: Initial core app-config: daily, hints, infinite, timeTrial, and ui knobs with sane defaults.
changelog.why: Row 7 core schemas - a fresh clone runs on these defaults (Holy Law #6).
